drafts.label: Reply · free tutor needs path
drafts.body:
You have me on free 24/7 tutors in every language. I want that world.

Where I push back a little: equalizer only holds if the tutor does not quietly do the thinking. If school still only grades the polished finish, free help becomes a cleaner shortcut. I'd rather score the messy attempts, not just the final sheet.
drafts.why: Grounded in free/24h/native language tutor. Take: equalizer needs process scoring. Love/I/I'd conversational.
drafts.tip: No invented tutor products; stay on OP equalizer claim + assessment path.

quality.notes: Caps; no em-dash; You/I contact; process bias; not house antithesis land. Attempt 3 after post-like fails.

drafts.label: Reply · news literacy as reps
drafts.body:
You named the hard one: screens connected, world not.

I do not think more content fixes it. News literacy is reps: stop, name the source, ask what would change your mind. Teachers already feel that. We should design practice around that pause, not another feed of current affairs slides.
drafts.why: Grounded in news vs noise + AI/social screens + teachers. Take: literacy = practiced pause. Different room from tutor equalizer.
drafts.tip: No invented conference details beyond OP IIMUN/teachers frame.

drafts.label: Short · feedback clocks (generalized)
drafts.body:
Fast feedback feels like progress. Sometimes it is.

Some skills need a slower clock: judgment, taste, when to trust a tool. If every loop closes in two seconds, you get fluency without depth. Match the feedback speed to the skill, or you train people to flinch at anything that takes real time.
drafts.why: Generalized practice/psych: feedback tempo vs skill type. Independent of free-tutor and news-literacy replies.
